'''Hernán Rodrigo López Mora''' (born 21 January 1978), also known as '''Rodrigo López''', is an Uruguayan [[Association football|football]] manager and former player who played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]].

López is the second maximum goal scorer of [[Football in Paraguay|Paraguayan football]] with 127 goals, behind [[Santiago Salcedo]] (152), and ahead of [[Juan Eduardo Samudio]] (119) and [[Fredy Bareiro]] (112).<ref name="hoy.com.py">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoy.com.py/deportes/sasa-vuelve-a-primera-con-general-de-mallorquin/amp|title = Diario HOY | Amparados bajo la bendición de la Cruz|date = 26 April 2016}}</ref>

==Club career==
Born in [[Montevideo]], López began his career with [[Club Atlético River Plate (Uruguay)|River Plate de Montevideo]] in Uruguay. He had short stints with [[Torino F.C.]] of Italy and [[AO Kavala]] of Greece in 1998 along with compatriot [[Pablo Gaglianone]]. In 2000, he joined [[Colo-Colo]] of Chile.

He returned to Uruguay in 2001 to play for [[Danubio FC]] and in 2002 he joined [[Racing Club de Montevideo]]

Between 2002 and 2004 he enjoyed a successful stint with [[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]] of [[Paraguay]] where he was part of the team that won both [[Copa Libertadores]] [[Copa Libertadores 2002|2002]] and [[Recopa Sudamericana|Recopa Sudamericana 2003]].

In 2004, he joined Mexican side [[Pachuca CF]] but after only a few games he returned to Paraguay to play for [[Club Libertad|Libertad]] where he scored an impressive 39 goals in 71 league games, won the [[Paraguayan Primera División|Primera División]] championship in 2006 and finished as the topscorer.

López returned to Mexican football in 2008 joining [[Club América]] where he played alongside a number of other South American players such as [[Federico Insúa]] of Argentina and [[Salvador Cabañas]].<ref>[http://southamerican-futbol.blogspot.com/2011/03/federico-insua-gambeta-vs-tecos.html Federico Insúa gambeta vs Tecos]</ref> He had a successful time with América, scoring a famous hat-trick against Tecos in the 2007 Apertura<ref>[http://southamerican-futbol.blogspot.com/2011/03/rodrigo-lopez-golazo-vs-tecos-apertura.html Rodrigo López golazo vs Tecos]</ref> and helping the team to win the 2008 [[InterLiga]].

In 2008, he joined [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] and had an unsuccessful start with the team, quickly reverted by contributing 11 goals in their championship season of [[Primera División Argentina 2008–09#Torneo Clausura|Clausura 2009]].<ref>[http://www.26noticias.com.ar/hernan-rodrigo-lopez-desde-tierras-uruguayas-llego-el-gran-goleador-92207.html 26 Minutos]. Retrieved 22 December 2009. {{in lang|es}}</ref>

López was bought by Argentine side [[Estudiantes de La Plata]] in June 2010 for a fee of around US$750,000.<ref>{{cite news|title=Con Rorro y el Torito |newspaper=Olé |date=26 June 2010 |url=http://www.ole.com.ar/estudiantes/Rorro-Torito_0_287371326.html |language=Spanish |accessdate=27 June 2010}}</ref> He scored a number of vital goals for the club in his first season helping the club to win the [[2010–11 Argentine Primera División season#Torneo Apertura|Apertura 2010]] tournament. He scored his first hat-trick for Estudiantes with three headers in a 5–1 win against Paraguayan side Guaraní in the group stages of the [[2011 Copa Libertadores]].<ref>[http://southamerican-futbol.blogspot.com/2011/03/rodrigo-lopez-golazo-conta-guarani.html Rodrigo López vs Guaraní]</ref> In the following game he scored the winning goal against league leaders Racing Club.<ref>[http://southamerican-futbol.blogspot.com/2011/03/hernan-rodrigo-lopez-vs-racing-clausura.html Hernán Rodrigo López vs Racing, Clausura 2011]</ref>

In July 2011, he signed a two-year contract with [[Club Atlético Banfield]].

One year later he returned to Paraguayan Football signing for [[Cerro Porteño]]. Then he was transferred to [[Sportivo Luqueño]] and now he is the main scorer of [[Club Libertad|Libertad]], being the topscorer at the [[2014 Paraguayan Primera División season#Torneo Apertura|2014 Apertura]], scoring 19 goals.

==International career==
On the youth level, López was runner-up with [[Uruguay national under-20 football team|Uruguay U-20]] at the [[1997 FIFA World Youth Championship]]. He even played the final against [[Argentina national under-20 football team|Argentina]].

López played a friendly match for [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] against [[China national football team|China]] in 1996.<ref name="Ole">[http://www.ole.clarin.com/notas/2009/08/21/futbolinternacional/01982936.html "La Celeste (y blanca)"] ''Olé''. Retrieved 21 August 2009. {{in lang|es}}</ref> Thirteen years later, in 2009, he was called again by coach [[Oscar Washington Tabárez]] for a friendly match against [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] and for the World Cup qualifying games against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]].<ref name="Ole"/> He was also part of the squad that achieved the qualification by defeating [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] on the playoff. However, he was not part of the Uruguayan squad that played the World Cup.

On 27 July 2010, he was called up to play a friendly match against [[Angola national football team|Angola]] in [[Lisbon]].

==Coaching career==
Following the departure of [[Celso Ayala]], López was appointed manager of Paraguayan club [[Sportivo Luqueño]] on 3 March 2020.<ref>[http://www.tigosports.com.py/futbol/sportivo-luqueno-hernan-rodrigo-lopes-nuevo-dt Hernán Rodrigo López, flamante DT de Luqueño], tigosports.com.py, 3 March 2020</ref> After the club saw the departure of as many as 11 players to transfers and contract dissolutions mid-tournament, López decided to resign from his position on 7 September 2020,<ref>http://www.tigosports.com.py/futbol/hernan-rodrigo-lopez-deja-la-conduccion-tecnica-de-luquenho , tigosports.com.py, 7 September 2020</ref> but agreed to coach his club for one last match, a come-from-behind 2–1 victory against [[Club River Plate (Asunción)|River Plate]] on 11 September 2020.<ref>http://www.tigosports.com.py/copa-de-primera/rodrigo-lopez-y-su-ultima-funcion-como-dt-auriazul-0 , tigosports.com.py, 11 September 2020</ref> During his short tenure as head coach of [[Sportivo Luqueño]], the team achieved 16 points in 12 matches (4W-4D-4L), climbing several positions in the table.
